product_title: WALNEW Sleeve Case for 6.8-inch All-New Kindle Paperwhite 11th Generation 2021, Protective Pouch Bag Case Cover for 6.8” Kindle Paperwhite E-Reader (Khaki)
review_text:
I don’t like to use a cover for my new Kindle Paperwhite as I like its naked weight and feel. However, it seems vulnerable when lying on the table or in a bag.
I saw this WALNEW Sleeve Case and it looked like it fit my needs. Simple and inexpensive protection.
.
My only concern was whether the Pop Socket would make the Kindle too tight of a fit. Fortunately, my fears were unfounded.
The Kindle slides in snugly and won’t slide out easily. It’s like a credit card sliding into and out of the slot in your wallet. The Pop Socket obviously makes a bulge in the case. I think having the Pop Socket on the backside of the case is best as I typically will lay the case down with the flap facing up. That way the screen is up and the Pop Socket is down on the hard table surface. It doesn’t sit flat, but that’s fine. Also, it is easier to insert the Kindle and not have the Pop Socket catch on the front edge of the case. You can avoid that on the flap as the Kindle goes into the case first then the Pop Socket passes the flap edge, which you can swing back out of the way.
.
I slide the Kindle in top-first. The Power button is then at the flap end and that ensures the button is not accidentally activated on full insertion. I think that’s a minor risk as the sewn lapped edge at the bottom of the case tapers up to full depth and isn’t going to touch the button when you push the Kindle fully down in the case. There’s plenty of clearance for the power button to the folded “hinge” of the flap and I can guarantee not to touch the button sliding the Kindle in that way.
.
The material inside the case is a fabric lining. It is not a soft velour-type material, so the Kindle is not cushioned a great deal. I would have perhaps preferred a microfiber-type surface against my Kindle! The flap appears to have a stiff layer sewn inside it, unlike the rest of the case. My guess is it is cardboard, based on the sounds it makes when you flex it. I suggest not folding the flap as it will likely end up wrinkled with a crease in it (as another reviewer mentioned) or a crack! I had a winter hat that had a peak just like that! I’m surprised a hard material layer wasn’t sewn into one face of the case, to protect the screen from point pressure. That would be a nice feature.
The two magnets do a good job of holding the flap closed. They are small and won’t harm the electronics at all.
There’s no branding on the case, which surprises me, but I think this is likely a generic case, made in China, which several vendors will offer.
.
The overall construction is excellent and the outer material feels very durable. I’m sure that, with time, the case material will soften up and the Kindle will be a slightly looser fit. Its function will not be affected though.
.
CONCLUSION:
I can recommend this case. 😊
At $15, it is a good quality, well-made item at an affordable price. And it fulfills its basic function of protecting yours and my Pop Socketed Kindle from scratches and minor drops.

review_text:
I got this memory card for my Samsung Galaxy Note 4. Some people may consider it an outdated phone, but it is still running strong for me. The only issue I had was with running out of storage space. The internal storage is 32GB and I had the [[ASIN:B00IVPU7AO Samsung EVO 64GB]] for external. While the 64GB card did the job, video files fill it up fast.

I’ve had issues using SanDisk Ultra on Galaxy phones in the past, so I was a little unsure how well this PNY would work. Thankfully it’s been working like a charm so far. Much faster write speeds than [[ASIN:B01DOB6YW4 Samsung’s 128GB EVO Select]] (90MB/s vs. 20 MB/s), as well as slightly faster read speeds (95MB/s vs. 80 MB/s).

While you are paying more for the PNY than the EVO, you get the faster transfer speeds. That said, if transfer speeds are your thing, then you can compare the PNY to the higher end [[ASIN:B01DOB6YUQ Samsung 128GB PRO Select]]. With the PRO, you are getting the same speeds as the PNY (90MB/s Write and 95MB/s Read), but the PRO comes at an even higher cost. So in that sense, the PNY is a better budged solution if fast transfer speeds are what you are looking for.

Just be sure your phone or tablet (or other device) supports the size card you are getting. Some older devices might not be able to handle 128GB or above. Thankfully my Note 4 did, and so far, I’m quite satisfied with this card.

product_title: PNY 1TB PRO Elite Class 10 U3 V30 microSDXC Flash Memory Card - 100MB/s, Class 10, U3, V30, A2, 4K UHD, Full HD, UHS-I, micro SD
review_text:
I just bought another one of these cards after having a good experience with PNY Pro Elite microSDXC cards in my smartphones and just ran two different tests using the latest version of CrystalDiskMark using two different card readers I have.
The first card reader is a Kingston MobileLite Plus USB 3.2 microSDHC/SDXC UHS-II Card Reader.
The second card reader is a Cable Matters Dual Slot USB C Card Reader (Model Number 201058).
I will list the ASIN numbers for each card at the end of my review for easier searching.

I cannot be sure if the card readers are limiting the ability of the microSDXC card to reach full advertised speeds or not. All I know is I get slightly different results with the two different card readers while plugged directly into a USB 3.2 Gen2 port on the back of my AsRock X570 Taichi desktop PC motherboard running the latest chipset drivers. Please note that the Kingston card reader has a USB-A type connector while the Cable Matters card reader has a USB-C type connector. However, the USB A and USB C ports that I used on my motherboard were right next to each other and again, both rated for USB 3.2 Gen2 speeds. My motherboard USB ports are rated for that USB protocol. The microSDXC card and the card readers are not. Please see my pics for the test results. The read and write speeds were within +/- 2-3 MB/s of advertised sequential read/write speeds with both card readers. I doubt anyone would notice the difference in real world applications unless you are doing time critical file transfers often. For the average consumer I'd say these cards seem to have a good price to performance ratio, especially when on sale. I can easily recommend these cards to friends and family and I do. Hope this helps you make a better buying decision. A good alternative to these cards to consider that are slightly better in advertised read speeds and potentially around the same price are the Sandisk Extreme brand microSDXC cards with ASIN number B07FCR3316. Those are rated to have a read speed of 160 MB/s with the same write speed of the PNY Pro Elite at 90 MB/s. The pricing seems to be within $5-10 of each other, so not much difference.
The Kingston card reader's ASIN number is B085P5FDXQ.
The Cable Matters card reader's ASIN number is B01KXWIHZY.
claim: I doubt anyone would notice the difference in real world applications unless you are doing time critical file transfers often. For the average consumer I'd say these cards seem to have a good price to performance ratio, especially when on sale.

review_text: I have two televisions in my house and first purchased Amazon's top seller in flat indoor antennas by  Gesobyte for less than 30 bucks. Then I watched some YouTube videos by the "antenna man," who railed against the inexpensive antenna and highly recommended this one. So, I purchased it for my second TV. Not only was it much more difficult to attach to the antenna port on the back of my TV, it was far less effective. After trying multiple multiple positions, removing the amplifier, and rescanning after each step, the best It did was 71 channels. They unfortunately weren't clear. I ordered another inexpensive one similar to the Gesobyte (which is no longer available), and it did significantly better. I then learned that I have to pay for postage to send the inferior but more expensive Channel Master back, which is aggravating. If you're in a metro area close to many towers like I am, don't be duped into thinking you have to pay more to get more channels or better quality!

product_title: Plugable USB 3.0 Sharing Switch for One-Button Swapping of USB Device or Hub Between Two Computers (AB Switch)
review_text:
Pretty decent USB3 switch. No issues with the USB3 switching functionality itself. The selected system sees the plugged in devices just fine, and the non-selected system just acts as though the devices have been unplugged. I just wish this switch had a remote that came with it. It's really inconvenient to have this switch on your desk with all the cabling since the two system ports are on the back while the device port is on the front... especially when the 2 cables which go to the systems are only 3 feet long. Fortunately, this switch is easily modified to have a remote. Since I've added the remote, the USB3 switch can sit under my desk with the other wires, and the switch sits on my desk in easy reach without the mess of all the USB cables.

The buttons on this switch pull the signal low (tie it to ground) when they're pressed. To add a remote, I just got a length of bundled 3 wire 24 gauge wires, a Single Pole Double Throw (SPDT) switch.. like these: [[ASIN:B00ZWWZ8CG E Support Heavy Duty 20A 125V 15A 250V SPST 3 Terminal Pin (ON)-OFF-(ON) Momentary Rocker Toggle Switch Metal Bat Pack of 5]].. then soldered 1 wire to ground, and 1 wire to each switch on the USB switch. At the other end, the ground wire was tied to the middle pole on the switch, and each of the other wires was tied to one of the throws on the switch. The best part is that the buttons on the pluggable USB switch still work. The remote just allows you to act as though you hit the button on the switch itself. Pluggable -- please add a remote to your product! I've included some pictures so you can see how I modified it to have a remote.

Keep in mind, you'll void your warranty doing this, and could possibly cause damage to the plugged in systems or devices if you don't know what you're doing. I take no responsibility for you modifying a USB switch to try to replicate what I have done.
claim: The selected system sees the plugged in devices just fine, and the non-selected system just acts as though the devices have been unplugged. the two system ports are on the back while the device port is on the front... especially when the 2 cables which go to the systems are only 3 feet long.

review_text: [[VIDEOID:5d9f50b7c93e9b038061df121a7a15a2]] I bought this so I could easily share my work computer's monitor, mouse, keyboard, ethernet and speakers with my personal laptop that I bring from home. It's a little annoying that I have to have two different gadgets and all of their associated cables to make this happen.  I would love to see plugable integrate the switch capability into the docking station itself, but all in all I can't really complain because it works. product_title: trueCABLE Cat6A Shielded Riser (CMR), 1000ft, Green, 23AWG Solid Bare Copper, 750MHz, PoE++ (4PPoE), ETL Listed, Overall Foil Shield (FTP), Bulk Ethernet Cable
review_text:
If you are looking for top quality CAT6A CMR indoor cable at a reasonable price, then you just found it.

I install Wi-Fi networks and camera systems and this particular cable is meant for an inside Wi-Fi AP/Switch/Router/Server installation. When I made my choice, I went by the following criteria:

• The cable must be solid copper. Many of the runs I install are up to 300 feet. Stranded copper should not be used past 75 feet.
• The cable must be CAT6A since the network I will be installing will, in the future, require 10G Ethernet over copper out to the maximum possible distance limitation of 328 feet.
• The cable must be properly documented so I can select the proper connector to use with it. I will not trust cable this is not fully documented up front.
• The cable must meet all EIA/TIA specifications and if used inside walls (not plenum air spaces) then it must further be CMR rated so it does not promote the spread of a fire.

Fortunately, trueCABLE (unlike many others) has properly published the specifications on the cable and I selected the Platinum Tools ezEX-44 unshielded connector. Since this connector is specific to Platinum Tools, you are also required to use the ezEX0 crimp tool and interchangeable die system. The two most critical specifications needed are the OD or outside diameter of the cable jacket and the OD of the conductor insulation, which basically means the copper conductor diameter PLUS accounting for the insulation around the conductor. It is NOT enough that a connector says “CAT6A compatible”, nor is it enough that a particular connector says it will work with “23 AWG” conductors. Each cable manufacturer will have different ODs for the cable and conductors. In this case, the cable OD is 7.30mm and the OD of the conductor insulation is 1.02mm. Very few connectors on the market will work with such a thick cable OD of 7.30mm, so careful research was necessary. When I selected the connector, I needed to know what the connector would accept and as it turns out, Platinum Tools also properly documents their connectors. The ezEX-44 accepts cable ODs up to 7.36MM and conductor OD range of 1.0 – 1.12mm. Perfect! This connector has the added advantage that it is pull-through in design and does not use load bars, plus the conductors stagger 4 high and 4 low to minimize near and far end cross talk, which is critical for high bandwidth applications. See my pictures for how this looks.

Taking the cable off the spool, this stuff is stout. The jacket is thick and the interior of the cable has a “spline” which separates the pairs to minimize cross talk. The spline further helps with keeping the cable from kinking while running it. There is a rip cord inside the cable, but I did not make use of that. You should use a cable stripper when terminating cable to RJ45 connectors. For such a thick cable, you are well advised to get a heavy-duty adjustable stripper such as the “Big Red” or BR-1 type. I took pictures of the inside of the cable.

Overall, I am impressed with the quality of this cable! I wrote a long review here with pictures because this product really deserves it.

Oh, and this was all at a lower price than Vertical Cable’s similar offering. I have used Vertical Cable and while they are comparable in quality, their cable costs more.

The spline further helps with keeping the cable from kinking while running it. There is a rip cord inside the cable, but I did not make use of that.

review_text: I teach computer networking in a program that requires students to make their own ethernet cables and make their own runs every semester. we still tend to use Cat5e just because it's cost effective and easy to work with for beginners but we do occasionally get Cat6 in and use it as it becomes available. I figured Cat6a would be no different from 6 so I decided to somewhat futureproof my house by buying this product for a home project I'm working in. this Cat6A stuff is a whole other animal if you are used to working with Cat5e or Cat6. the cable is THICK, like RG6 Coax cable thick. I was worried my cat 6 connectors I had on hand wouldn't work so I decided to  terminate the roll. I had to manually reduce tension on my cable strippers because they just don't open up enough for this cable. the cable coloring isn't the worst I've seen but it's not the clearest either as far as separating your whites/solids and which white is for which pair. the wires themselves are pretty on-par with cat6 which is to say much heavier gauge than your typical Cat5e. I could barely get the wires into my 3-piece cat6 RJ45 connector and I had to pinch, smash, and otherwise cram the cable jacket into the RJ45(even after I cut out the center shielding). I'm not sure if this is just an issue with this particular product or if all Cat6a cable is made to this standard, but just so you're warned you'll need at least a decent level of practice to work with it. I can usually do a 3-piece termination on Cat5e in about a minute to a minute and a half, this took about 3 or 4 minutes so it's going to take a bit more time than you're used to if you tend to work with the older, cheaper standards.

review_text:
A lot of these cheap webcams use very small sensors and rely on super wide optics to see the room. They also tend to overstate their resolving power, claiming to send a 1080 sized image that looks more like an upscaled 480. I'm happy to say this is a degree better than those!
The sensor is still small, as expected, but the optics aren't super wide to the point that edges distort. In fact, it seems pretty rectilinear (straight lines stay relatively straight in the background). The resolution seems decent as well. I'm not sure if it's actually resolved a full HD image like it claims, but it is definitely more resolution than a lot of the cheaper webcams I've tried. It looks pretty good and I'd argue that any live web call, skype, zoom, etc, will look perfectly fine with this camera and play at whatever resolution that protocol is capable of clearly.
The thing that sorta disappointed me, however, was the "ring light" built in. I mean, I have a REAL ring light so I get what that should do, but this sorta does... nothing. It doesn't create soft shadows or a circular catch light in my eyes- in fact, it's very hard to discern the difference between capture with the light on versus off. In a dark room, it can add a bit of illumination to the subject to make you a little easier to see, but it really isn't all that bright and under normal lighting conditions in my office, it makes zero difference at all. It also seems to get kind of warm as long as it is plugged in, even if not currently active, so I'm going to be in the habit of disconnecting it when not using, and only plugging it in when I need to make a video call at my desk.
For what it is, it is definitely a better webcam than most of the cheap ones, but it definitely is not perfect!

I will likely put an additional 2 tb SSD in this in the near future, but, the 512 gb drive that it comes with is doing great. I have some external drives I can connect for excess storage if needed in the mean time.

If you are looking for a compact computer that runs Windows 10 and can handle media well, this is a good bet. I am very happy with it. I have mine set up as a dedicated Digital Audio Workstation and it is working great in that capacity.

product_title: Patriot LX Series Micro SD Flash Memory Card 128GB - 5 Pack
review_text:
I purchased the 5-pack of 32GB microSD cards and am still in the process of testing all 5. So far they seem to work fine. Like all flash storage, they start out faster when they are empty and get slower the closer they get to full. These start out at ~50MB/s write but quickly drop to ~20MB/s write after roughly 10-20% full. Overall, while sustaining write and filling the storage they average 18MB/s. That's nearly double the advertised 10MB/s write speed. I'm seeing ~72MB/s reading the card when verifying. Read speed was not advertised so there is nothing to compare to. It is rare to see a product underpromise and overdeliver, especially when it comes to data storage, so this is a welcome surprise.

These came preformatted as FAT32 and 32GB is small enough that the built-in format tool for Windows will allow reformatting them as FAT32 without any tricks (at least, as of Windows 10). I bought these for use in my Krikzz Everdrives (64 X7, GB X7, and GBA Mini) since ROMs for those systems do not take up much space there was no need for larger ones.

While these are certainly not the fastest cards on the market they never claimed to be and are pretty decent overall, especially for the price. While the use cases for 32GB cards are getting narrower and narrower if you do not need a ton of space these are great.

I cannot comment as to the write durability of the cards as I just got them. If I do not come back to update this review you can safely assume they are still working fine. Do note though that in my use case I am writing infrequently so it won't be the best measure of durability in write-heavy scenarios.

Testing was done using a Sabrent USB 3 card reader (B00OJ5WBUE).
claim: Can see 5

review_text:
While some people are complaining about this purchase, I had no issues.

Capacity: All five drives are 58.2 GB capacity and all five drives were able to be filled and tested to capacity. While some people are complaining that this is not "64 GB", this is standard. Windows calculates 1 KB as 1024 bytes. Drive manufacturers calculate it as 1000 bytes. Technically this should equal 61 GB, so yes, it is a little low, but not below standard IMO.

Failure Rate: If you look back to the reviews for these drives when Patriot first released them, there was a high amount of failures, so it is what it is. If that happens, return or exchange your product, but it doesn't necessarily mean it's "fake".

Speed: Patriot claims a minimum of 10mbps on their site. My experience was that on an old monitor port on USB2 I only achieved 10mbps even with a good reader, but when connected directly to a USB3 port with a good reader I achieved 30+ mbps with all cards (using large files).

See the photos for details. The TeraCopy transfers are each on a different drive. Will buy again. The seller I purchased from was "Highly Anticipated Electronics" for those of you worried about fakes.

product_title: Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount
review_text:
Sony's latest 4K UHD TV for 2018 is quite a lot to take in at 55", but it definitely makes every inch count. Having been in electronics sales in the past I have kept up with most of the newest models of TVs. Sony has continued to differentiate itself from most of its competitors by manufacturing commercial grade, cutting edge TVs and monitors for customers who demand the ultimate TV experience, regardless of cost. If you strictly look at this model based on cost you will not find it very competitive. If you make comparisons based upon pure performance though, this product really can't be beat.

As you would expect, the real measure of a TV's quality is in the picture and to a lesser extent in the sound. Insofar as sound is concerned, this model has one of the better, louder speakers that I have seen on a flat panel TV. While the internal speakers will definitely not please hard core audiophiles it definitely provides better performance than most TVs you will find on the market right now. For me, the best way to experience sound with this TV is via the Bluetooth feature though. You can easily connect your Bluetooth headphones or speakers to this unit in the set up menu.

Video quality is flat-out stunning. I would say that it rivals many current models of OLEDs that I have seen of the same size. Saturation and color depth are greatly enhanced by its auto adjustment to ambient light. Pictures are extremely bright and crisp. The contrast of black to white is the best I have seen of any flat panel TV, including OLEDs. Whatever steps Sony has taken to improve LED/LCD backlighting technology has really paid off in a big way. When you come across a scene where the screen is totally black you can honestly not tell whether the TV is still on or not. There are also a lot of fine tuning adjustments for video that can drastically improve the picture for your particular installation.

I used a variety of HD and 4K inputs with this model and they all worked as expected. Although not in 4K, broadcast TV pictures look amazing as do most other forms of HD content. Sony's upscaling technology has improved to the point where it is really becoming difficult to tell the difference between native 4K video and HD video that has been upscaled to 4K. Between the upscaling and rapid 120Hz refresh rate most HD video really pops on this model. It is especially apparent in live sports broadcasts and action scenes.

Sony's interface to TV programming is, unfortunately, a bit weaker in terms of quality. It uses a customized Android TV OS, which is really just a stripped-down version of Android. While the chipset Sony uses is fast enough to keep the interface running reasonably snappy, the various apps that come with it are all over the map in terms of quality. Some of the viewing apps can get painfully slow or even crash completely. I was unable to get the HBO Go app to work at all. At least once I had to restart the TV due to a crashed Android TV app. There is a bare minimum of memory (8GB) that is available for storage which makes the TV impossible to use as a DVR or to pause live TV. If you want a full-blown DVR and multimedia suite that is simple to use and very robust, you would be better off connecting an external computer or quality Android TV box than using the internal interface. You will also have to manually search through and install individual Android apps if you want to stream video from your NAS or connected storage. This functionality really should be included in the main interface as it is a pain to hunt down individual apps like VLC and a file browser that supports SMB. Android is great when it comes to having a wide array of apps available to run. Dealing with dozens of different apps with varying levels of quality and limited support can often be a pain though.

Along with the TV, I also took advantage of Sony's free 5 day preview of its Sony Playstation VUE service, which you can run as an Android app on the TV. Insofar as streaming services go, VUE does not have the greatest programming or prices on the market. It does provide a very high quality stream though. So, you can easily sit through entire movies without the typical pain of buffering and lost frames. The big let down with this service is the fact that you can not utilize the feature that lets you rewind all of the programs on live TV for 30+ minutes. This is a big selling point of the service, but you can't take advantage of it with the app that comes with this TV. Personally, I have found DirecTV's DirecTVNOW service to be the best of the streaming choices available at the moment. Unfortunately, the app for this service does not appear to work with SONY TV's, unless you are using an external TV input. Still, you can choose from several others like Amazon Video, HULU, Netflix, DISH Network, etc.

The overall build quality of the hardware is excellent, with a very slim bezel and attractive black trim. The included stand does an adequate job of holding up the TV, but does not seem stable enough to support the set in the event of an earthquake, which we have plenty of here in California. I would highly suggest using a quality wall mount instead if there is any chance that the TV could be bumped into or shaken.

I was not very impressed with the remote. The navigation buttons are rather small and grouped too close to the other buttons. You need to use the navigation (up, down, left, right) buttons to do pretty much everything, yet they are one of the smallest buttons on the remote. This is fine if you are using another device for most of your viewing and do not need to use the Sony remote that often, but it definitely is not a selling point. I never tried the voice command features on the remote. I'm one of those people who doesn't like speaking to inanimate objects though. i am uploading a picture of the remote, since it isn't shown on the product page.

Overall, this model provides a great viewing experience. Coupled with a quality sound system, it can be the basis of an incredible home theater. While the programming interface isn't the best, at least you have the option of using an external device instead. If you already have cable box, DVR or a satellite tuner you will probably rarely utilize the Sony interface anyway. If you want the best of both worlds, I would suggest running a 4K connection directly from a dedicated Windows 10 PC that includes a TV tuner card, Blu-Ray drive and access to plenty of storage. Along with software like KODI you can build a multimedia collection that is almost limitless when it comes to the variety of multimedia options you have at your disposal.

review_text:
Pros:

$Price is very competitive.

Picture quality is outstanding. I bought this TV for the full array 4k picture and it delivers.

Cons:

Android operating system and interface is horrible and worse is the remote. Google OS starts with you having to accept multiple privacy policies and accept Google access permissions to your data. It is loaded with bloatware that cannot be uninstalled. Default app settings allow access permissions to all data, photos, contacts etc. So you have to disable and disallow permissions. To get to my favorite app, I have to arrow right 10 times. These unwanted apps can't be removed or hidden.

The unforgiving remote is loaded with tiny buttons that I have to use my nail to press. This makes accuracy difficult. If you press the wrong button you will have to wait 60 seconds for the remote to respond to "back". Another annoyance is the volume control doesn't work on the remote if you have a sound bar. You have to use a separate remote.

Within Android OS, there is no network speed test feature. I've been troubleshooting 4k and have no visibility of speed to know what speed works during varying fios speeds throughout the day. The powerline adapters has made 4k viewable where wifi fell short.

If you don't need a wired connection, a workaround is to plug in a Roku 4k stick, tried and true, works much better than the clunky Android Interface and Sony remote. The external Roku stick is superior for the interface and simple remote configuration. It also offers speed test for wifi. This also allows for changing TVs, just take your loaded/pre-configured Roku stick to another TV. Roku 4k Streaming Stick remote also allows for one remote operation with volume control. Note: You must configure the settings individually for each HDMI port and for the Smart TV Streaming apps. We are streaming 4k over 5G if speeds are optimal, fios speeds slow during peak use hours. Less than 75Mbps will not stream 4k very well.

Another challenge is the sound system which requires purchasing of an add-on HD rear speakers and sound bar to give a theater sound. The Sony sound bar gives great sound and offers a discount if purchased with the TV.

product_title: Lightdow 420-800mm f/8.3 Manual Zoom Super Telephoto Lens + T Mount Ring for Nikon D3500 D5600 D7500 D500 D600 D700 D750 D800 D850 D3200 D3400 D5100 D5200 D5300 D7000 D7200 Camera (White Version)
review_text:
If you have read the other reviews you will understand that there are limitations to this lens, but don't let that discourage you. Keep in mind that the biggest aspect here was the price. I actually had fun trying this out today. You're going to need a bright day because the aperture is fixed according to the focal length. For example, at 420mm the aperture is fixed at f8.3. As you increase the focal length, the aperture gets smaller until you get to 800mm where the aperture is fixed at f16. If you are interested in purchasing this lens, please read the special note that you need to use this lens in the manual mode on your camera.

Remember, this lens is less than $100, so we are talking about something worthwhile for those who just simply enjoy photography.

That said, I took several photos from a nearby location. The one where the heron is looking to the left is using the Canon 75-300mm at 300mm. The photo looking toward the exit sign was with the Canon 18-55mm at 40mm. I took these to compare this lens with those that have auto focus. All the photos but one are unedited (except for size) and the ISO was set to 100.

I was very impressed with how the lens performed for one of this price range. It will take some practice and patience learning to focus manually, but it will pay off. As recommended in other reviews, use the live view on your camera and use a remote (or at least 10 seconds on the timer) to reduce camera shake. You have to remember that not only are you magnifying the subject, but also any movement.

Unfortunately, it was so bright that I couldn't really see the LCD screen to focus (I think I could have gotten the images sharper), so I had to do the best I could with focusing through the viewfinder. But still, I was happy with the results. With patience (required regardless) and some editing, I think you'll be pleased.

There will be some chromatic aberrations, which is to be expected, but with some photo editing (such as Light Room Classic), you should be able to clear that up.

Overall, this lens performed as was advertised. It comes with an EOS adapter, which is metal instead of plastic (a plus!). The lens also comes in a bag. After a few minutes of practice attaching the adapter and then attaching the lens to the camera, I felt very comfortable. I keep the extra quick release adapter that came my tripod on all the time.

If you want to have some fun with telephoto photography, then this lens is definitely worth getting!

The photo of the jet was taken without the use of a tripod. The camera was set to AV so I only had to concentrate on focusing. I figure the jet was at about 28,000 feet but I could tell what type of flight it was. With $30 of the price you can’t go wrong!
claim: If you have read the other reviews you will understand that there are limitations to this lens, but don't let that discourage you. Keep in mind that the biggest aspect here was the price. I actually had fun trying this out today. You're going to need a bright day because the aperture is fixed according to the focal length.

product_title: Metra TYTO-01 JBL Amplifier Interface Harness & Metra 70-8114 Steering Wheel Control Wire Harness with RCA for 2003-Up Select Toyota/Scion/Lexus Vehicles
review_text:
I was pulling my hair out trying to replace the factory head unit in my 2003 Toyota 4Runner that came with the factory JBL audio system (amp and sub in trunk). I was minutes away from just driving my truck off a cliff out of frustration with how many different poorly documented factory wiring options there were for one freaking make/model of car. This was my 4th wiring harness I purchased and the only one that worked. It works perfect. Please note however the product does not match the picture in the description. There are no RCA cables at all, and the black box is a different shape see the attached picture. However, it seems to work fine by hooking up the eight wire leads instead of four RCA's.

I will explain what was wrong with the other three harnesses, as I figure people with the same vehicle as me may be running into the same issues and this is the answer.

1st attempt - Metra 70-1761 - This is the standard Toyota 87+ wire harness, however if you have a JBL factory headunit these wires will not fit. This is for non JBL headunits, that only have 4 door speakers. I had to remove 6 panels and take my dash half apart to get to see these factory wires.

2nd attempt - Metra 70-8113 - Fit one of the three factory JBL harnesses, and the new head unit powered on, however no sound. Found out part of my factory JBL system was an amp in the trunk that powers 10 speakers. This harness didn't provide the necessary data signal to the amp to turn it on, so there was no sound. The blue "amp on" wire did not work.

3rd attempt - Metra 70-8117 Amp Bypass Harness - Decided the bypass the amp and center/tweeters all together and just hook up the 4 door speakers with this bypass harness. It did not fit the factory harnesses, and with some extensive googling for wiring guides i found out the specific model factory headunit i had (JBL 56827) has three plugs on it, however none of these 40 some wires work for bypassing. They are all for audio-in expansions and steering control and other stuff. This is about where I lost it.

4th attempt - This - It doesn't look at all like the picture. There are no RCA connections as pictured, and the black box is completely different. My new headunit had RCA connections which made me think this was not going to work. I figured it was worth a shot though so I wired it up to the 8 F/R L/R speaker leads. IT WORKED! It was sounding a bit distorted so I tweaked the attenuator knob and now it sounds incredible and clear. product_title: SMSL Q5 Pro Digital Amplifier 2-50W USB/Coaxial/Optical with Remote Control - Black
review_text:
The reason for buying this amp was to build a better sound system for music to be used with my iMac computer. My older Klipsch computer speaker setup stopped working, and my goal was to step away from speakers specifically designed for the computer and create a much bigger and better sound. I ordered the SMSL Q5 Pro from Amazon and a set of factory refurbished Polk Audio TSi100 bookshelf speakers straight from Polk. I held off on ordering a sub, but chose this amp in part because of the dedicated sub out.

The amp is compact and appears to be very nicely built. Sturdy aluminum case. Very easy to use and work your way through the input options. Treble and bass settings are not on separate knobs, but are easily accessed with a click in of the volume. Bass and treble then appear on the lcd screen and are adjusted by turning the volume knob.

Sound reproduction is very nice. The Polk speakers I am using are 8ohm. The amp delivers 45 watts per channel when using 8ohm speakers. The end result, thus far, is very very good. Plenty of power to really push the speakers if you like to listen at higher volumes. Amp delivers a good amount of low end....even without a sub. I have both the bass and treble set at +7 (+9 is max). Music is crisp with punchy lows.

I didn't find a bunch of reviews of folks using this just for computer setups....so I wanted to give my opinion on using it for this purpose only. Have only had it hooked up for a short period of time, but so far....I very much would recommend it. Of course, your choice of quality speakers make a huge difference as well.

I will update when/if something changes or when I add a powered sub into the mix.

UPDATE: Added a super compact powered sub into the system. Came across the 300 watt Polk Audio PSW111 8" powered sub on Craigslist locally. Couldn't pass up the price on a mint condition piece. Using the dedicated sub out on the SMSL into the LFE input on the sub, I added it into the mix. Let me just say...straight away I was pleasantly surprised with the output from the amp. I was able to dial the bass down to 2 and let the Polk TSi100 bookshelf speakers handle primarily the mids and highs while the sub handles the low end. I'm still hooked up only to the iMac using the USB connection, and the sound is now what I would consider audiophile great. Plenty of power to drive the speakers and more than enough for the sub.

I ran it hard for well over an hour to test and really explore the capabilities. One thing that I read in other reviews was how warm the amp got. I must say that mine got just a little warm to the touch, but not close to what I would call hot. Much cooler than I really expected. My big Denon network receiver used for surround sound gets down right hot when pushed hard for that long.

So.....in summary, using the SMSL Q5 Pro with Polk Audio TSi100 bookshelf speakers and a Polk Audio PSW111 compact powered subwoofer connected to my iMac using the USB connection....could not be happier. Crisp and punchy with power to spare. I would highly recommend.

I have it paired with a Mac Mini using optical output and bluetooth dongle for tablet or Echo Dot. The sound is quite flat and not colored. I am driving a pair of British brand bookshelf speakers and an Energy 8" powered sub. Really satisfied. However there are only few things to be desired.

I would have loved to have a variable sub out in crossover frequency and output. Also I would had appreciated a USB A port to connect the bluetooth dongle. Also the equalizer settings are a complete mystery and useless for the most part.

Things to be cautious of are: make sure you use banana plugs for speakers and avoid bare cable or spades as much as you can. A short in this type of amplifier can be catastrophic. In the same line, I did connect all plugs that were needed (optical, speakers, sub, 3.5mm, power brick) before connecting the AC adapter to the wall. That way you make sure you don't short or create any potential shorts.

product_title: Bang & Olufsen Beoplay E8 3rd Generation True Wireless in-Ear Bluetooth Earphones, with Microphones and Touch Control, Wireless Charging Case, 35-Hour Playtime, Green
review_text:
Bang & Olufsen Beoplay E8 3rd Generation True Wireless earphones come with all accouterments you'd expect from a premium pair of truly wireless earbuds. In this package, you get a premium pair of earbuds, a leather charging case, additional ear tips, and a thick USB-C cable.

Where Bang & Olufsen distances themselves from the pack with the Beoplay E8 3rd gen is:
- Exceptional battery life
- Transparency Mode
- Bluetooth 5.1

-Battery Life
Bang & Olufsen claims their 60 mAh earphones can deliver up to 7 hours of talk time on a single charge if the volume is kept at a moderate level. Combine this with a 530 mAh charging case that can recharge these earphones 4 additional times on a single charge which delivers up to 35 hours of play assuming moderate volume.

In my testing, I cranked this headset to max volume and was still able to consistently receive 6-8 hours of continuous playback. The charging case delivered 4 full recharges for the headphones. I typically wore these earphones while at the gym. My gym sessions usually lasted between an hour and a half and two hours and I go to the gym 4 times a week. I averaged listening to music on this headset 7-8 hours per week and it took a full month for me kill the battery on this thing after its initial charge.

- Transparency Mode
Instead of attempting to cram active noise cancelling technology in their earphones, Bang & Olufsen uses what they call transparency mode instead. It has 4 levels ranging from off to level 3. What it essentially does is combine with the noise isolation you get from the ear tips (and I highly recommend you use the foam ones that are included) to reduce the playback volume by 25% at each step. When you activate level 3 music doesn’t play at all simulating the experience, you’d get from open-back headphones.

Having used ANC earbuds in the past I must say I have been less than impressed with them. IMHO, over-the-ear headphones are needed to deliver the best active noise cancelling experience and earbuds can only approximate a portion of what the former provides. Instead of being forced into using a flawed design, Bang & Olufsen uses a much more practical and effective design for their headphones. I just wish you could do more than turn it on and off with touch input.
- Bang & Olufsen App
I was a bit skeptical about installing the app after seeing its rating on both iOS and Android. On both platforms, the app has a 2 out of 5 rating. Still, I pushed forward because there was an update available right away and I hoped there were improvements made to the app. However, the main reason I installed the app is a significant part of your experience with these earphones is ‘hidden’ within the app.
For example, I mentioned transparency mode earlier. While you can turn transparency mode on and off with touch input, you can only access off and level 1 through this means. If you also want to use levels 2 and 3, you’ll have to do so via the app. Similarly, there are EQ settings for this headset that can only be accessed via the app. In fact, you can further customize an EQ setting as well but that too is only available through the app. Finally, the only way to get an accurate percentage of battery for these earphones is through the app.

What I liked about these earphones was:
- Premium build. This package is made of Leather, Aluminum, Polymer and Silicon. Combine those with an IP54 and you feel like you’re holding something that was designed to perform well and last for a good, long time.
- Listening experience. The listening experience gained from B&O tuning is legendary. B&O tuning has become such a coveted commodity that LG has released cellphones that included B&O tuning to help their organization deliver the best possible listening experience to their customers. With this headset you’re not just getting precision tuning you’re getting a frequency response of 20-20k Hz, 5.7mm drivers, 107dB sensitivity, 16ohm impedance and SBC, AAC and Aptx codecs. Coupled together, this set of earphones delivers a listening experience that rivals, and likely surpasses, most other headsets on the market.
- Battery life. The battery life of these earphones sets a new standard. I have tons of these true wireless earbuds; some include Airpods, Galaxy Buds, and the SoundCore Liberty 2 Pros. Most of those headsets deliver 4-6 hours of play on a single charge but only if you keep the volume at 50% or less. I almost always have the B&O’s at max volume, and I get almost twice as much usage out of them on a single charge and I only have to worry about charging the case once per month. Nothing else is even close.

What I disliked with these earphones was:
- Volume output. I had to keep the volume cranked up on this headset to deliver the volume I wanted. I also found transparency mode much more effective when these drivers were being pushed.
- Indicator light. While I appreciate that there was an indicator light that’s visible while the charging case was closed, the information a single dot can give is very limited.
- Product guide/manual. There is a ton of functionality built within the touch controls. For example, a long press on the left earbud lowers volume with the same action on the right earbud raises it. You can also access your smartphone’s voice assistant, skip and replay tracks but finding all of this out is unnecessarily involved. There are pages of the same text being written in multiple languages, so a user has to turn page after page just to get to a completed train of thought. This was very frustrating for me.

Overall, despite the drawbacks, Bang & Olufsen delivers a level of quality and innovation that sets their E8 3rd Generation true wireless earphones apart from the pack. These earphones sound great, are feature-rich and finally give true wireless headphones enough battery life to rival that of last generation wireless headsets that were connected by a single wire. 5 out of 5 rating for Bang & Olufsen’s E8 3rd Generation true wireless earphones.

product_title: Bang & Olufsen Beoplay E8 3rd Generation True Wireless in-Ear Bluetooth Earphones, with Microphones and Touch Control, Wireless Charging Case, 35-Hour Playtime, Green
review_text:
OVERALL IMPRESSIONS:

Elegant to look at first and foremost. Love the leather charging case.

The wireless Qi charging and USB-C option make this the most convenient among TWS for 2020.

You don’t need to download the app. Only if you want to customize the sound and rename the earbuds.

Super lightweight. With the correct earplug, it’s a joy to wear. Not to mention the aluminum and polymer combination makes this an elegant work of art in itself.

The charging case is real leather with chamfered edges. It's the most gorgeous wireless charging case I've seen and brings everyone else to their knees.

Love the IP54 rating. It's a true dust and sweat resistant earphone versus Apple's IPX4 rating only which doesn't make it dust-resistant.

Sound signature is a bit warm and lacks bass. This makes listening more pleasurable over extended periods but not ideal for today’s bass-heavy music like EDM and Rap.

You can adjust the overall music quality via the B&O app, but I still don't get a rich sound quality.

Downside is the lack of noise cancellation which I don’t care for but at this price point, it’s hard not to ask for it.

Here’s a comparison with the Apple AirPods Pro and AirPods:

1. Overall: AirPods Pro

In terms of sound quality, no adjustment needed. Full and bright for all genres.

Reaches loud volume with no distortion.

Works best with Apple devices and auto switches from phone to computer.

2. Runner up: TIE between AirPods 2.0 and BO E8 3.0.

AirPods has brighter sound. Best for rap and pop.

BO E8 3.0 has a warm sound signature best for relaxed/chill music genres. Less fatiguing vocals.

3. Best value: AirPods 2.0

Love the OG design more than the Pro. Don’t like stuff shoved in my ear canal. So I prefer it sitting outside. Doesn’t fit everyone though.

4. Best fit without falling off: TIE AirPods Pro and BO E8 3.0

Both are shoved in your ear. LOL. Both are light and barely noticeable IF you properly select the correct size for your ears. Improper selection can be annoying and also irritating over time.

5. Best for outdoor: BO E8 3.0

While the Pro is IPX4 meaning water resistant to a degree. The BO ups the ante with a dust rating of 5. Therefore IP54. And the new size and lighter weight from first 2 versions make this a great revision.

6. Best controls: B&O E8 3.0

Very sensitive touch controls. It's one that you need to get used to. I'd also love a BEEP feedback that can be turned on/off and volume adjusted in the app. Currently there is no feedback - sound or haptic - and that's a big miss.

With that aside, these have the best controls possible once you get used to it. From single taps (pause music, transparency mode), to two taps (track forward/back), to three taps (voice control and call control), and finally to a steady hold (volume control). It's impressive and beats everyone else in this game.

review_text:
I’ve tried these for a week now and it’s hard to put into context how great they are but here goes. I’m no audiophile but I love music and know what sounds good.

Prior to these I’d been using AirPods which I thought were great and they are but there really is no comparison to the sound quality with B&O.

The leather case is gorgeous and the buds fit nicely in there. The charging case worked on all four of my charging pads as well as the cord it came with. I charged them fully and after using for a good couple of hours a day I still have plenty of battery power. Do make sure they’re correctly fitted into the case so that it makes contact to charge.

It comes with a selection of different size ear buds and it took a bit of trial and error until I found the size that fits. I’ve danced around the house these in, blow dried my hair and hiked and they’ve stayed put. I personally wouldn’t run with these in. I’d be too worried about losing something so expensive.

The volume control which is done by touching the ear bud in the right ear is very sensitive. They both are actually and I’ve managed to pause and skip ahead when I’m putting my hair behind my ears. As for range I’ve used them at work and been a good 30’ from my phone and I haven’t lost the connection.

You can set personal sound preferences using the app. I prefer the “warm” setting and it’s useful to have a podcast setting for when you’re listening to audiobooks or a talk radio station.

My play list for when I’ve finished work that I titled “When I’ve had it up to here” has everything from classical to Queen to Justin Timberlake. Justin has never sounded so good. It’s simply amazing. I’m seriously blown away by the quality. It’s enough to bring you to tears. At full volume the sound stays in your ears. It doesn’t leak out to the people around you. A pet peeve when I’m on the train and I have to listen to the tinny sound leaking from someone else’s earbuds.

There are some bad reviews for the actual app but it’s been flawless for me. You can check the battery level, set and save your sound preferences and fiddle around with it until you’ve found your perfect sound.

I have a Bluetooth adaptor for when I’m flying (which is every week) and these work with that too so I never have to put up with inferior airline headsets or carry another pair.

As for value for money, what price amazing sound? That’s so subjective isn’t it. If you like great sound and have the budget, look no further than these

product_title: Bang & Olufsen Beoplay E8 3rd Generation True Wireless in-Ear Bluetooth Earphones, with Microphones and Touch Control, Wireless Charging Case, 35-Hour Playtime, Green
review_text:
Initially, I wasn't overly impressed with these earbuds. After spending a few days with them, my thoughts have changed. They have a truly amazing sound after the learning curve. First of all, I don't think the shape of my ears are very conducive to holding a pair of earbuds firmly, especially when these are a little heavier than inexpensive ones. Included are four assorted sizes of silicone tips and one pair of foam tips. None of them were an ideal match for me. I ended up sticking with the pair that was already attached when they first arrived. After a day or so of frustration from them repeatedly falling out, I decide to follow the instructions. When inserting, I start with the speaker side toward the back of my head and rotate rotate the speaker to the top of my head in a screwing fashion. You'll know you have a good seal when the outside world becomes muffled. If you don't get that seal, you're not going to have any bass.

Now, onto the sound. It's a totally flat response that many may consider uninspiring or harsh. I'm one of those who find it uninspiring, but this is how the signal comes from the source without tone shaping. I know this to be true because it sounds just like my audiophile receiver when engaging the tone bypass button. That's where downloading the B&O app comes in as a great tool. The equalizer is a disc with one button that can be moved around the disc to emphasize or cut frequencies to suit your individual tastes. Very simple and intuitive (see image). Some reviewers have complained about the lack of bass. With proper tone shaping and a good seal, you can get some overpowering bass from them without a hint of clipping. You can save multiple customized tones or choose from one of the manufacturer provided tones. The B&O app applies the tone setting to your favorite music player. I have three or four players loaded on my android and it works with all of them. One little quirk. If you kill the app, you may have to open the B&O app to select your tone again. I haven't downloaded the latest firmware, so this issue may have been corrected, or it may just be an idiosyncrasy unique to my phone. It only takes half a minute set it again, so it's no big issue with me.

The biggest downside to me is that you have to turn your phone location on to access settings within the app. I like to leave my location off because it's a battery drainer. At least it will retain your latest tone setting once you exit the app and turn your location back off. I don't think it's worth taking a star off for this, but it's somewhat of an annoyance. Why this app needs location information is a mystery to me.

Like I said at the beginning of my review, a learning curve is involved. You will accidentally hit the touch sensitive controls in the first few days but after a week of so, you'll get the hang of it. I have one suggestion for B&O. Please include an adapter. This only comes with a cable and seems to be a trend with a lot of manufacturers lately, but at this price, I'm sure buyers wouldn't mind paying five or ten bucks more for one.
Bottom line. If you're serious about your music and exercise a little patience getting to know this piece of technology, you will not be disappointed. I took some phone videos of Bob Seger and Heart concerts last year and watching these with the E8's in my ears made me feel like I was there all over again!
